title: M1L and M1R: the make-one increases
subtitle: Invisible increases that lift the bar between two stitches.
excerpt: M1L (make one left) and M1R (make one right) lift the bar of yarn running between two stitches and knit into it, producing a new stitch with no hole. The direction of the lean is controlled by which way the lifted loop is worked.
sourceNotes: Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), increases chapter. Weldon's Practical Knitter, Series 2 (1887).

glossaryTerms.definition: Make one left: a left-leaning invisible increase made by lifting the bar between stitches with the left needle from front to back, then knitting through the back loop to prevent a hole.
Make one right: a right-leaning invisible increase made by lifting the bar between stitches with the left needle from back to front, then knitting through the front loop.

content.text: M1L and M1R (abbreviated from 'make one left' and 'make one right') add stitches by lifting the strand that runs between the last worked stitch and the next stitch on the left needle, placing it on the left needle, and knitting into it. The direction of the lean depends on whether the lifted strand is picked up from the front or the back.

leans right. Used in pairs either side of a centre stitch or centre line, they produce a clean symmetrical increase that is nearly invisible in the finished fabric. Difficulty: intermediate, mainly because of the different pickup directions.
DK yarn and 4 mm needles with a few rows worked
Work to the point in the row where the increase is needed.
Insert the left needle tip under the bar between the last stitch and the next, picking it up from front to back.
Knit into the back loop of this lifted strand. This twists the stitch closed and prevents a hole.
Insert the left needle tip under the bar between stitches, this time from back to front (needle enters from the back, exits at the front).
Knit into the front loop of this lifted strand. Because the strand is seated with the correct leg forward, no twisting is needed.

M1L and M1R appear in pairs on either side of a central stitch in raglan increases, hat crown gussets, and seamless sweater yokes. They also appear singly on sleeve caps and sock gussets where a single left- or right-leaning increase is all that is needed. A common abbreviation pairing is 'k to 1 st before marker, M1R, k1, sm, k1, M1L' for a paired increase around a central stitch.

items.symptom: A small hole appears at the increase point
items.cause: Knitting M1L through the front loop rather than the back
items.fix: For M1L, always knit through the back loop. The back-loop entry twists the stitch closed. For M1R, the front-loop entry is correct.

items.symptom: Cannot identify the bar to lift
items.cause: The yarn strand between stitches is under slight tension
items.fix: After the last worked stitch, pull both needles slightly apart with both hands to open the gap and expose the strand.

items.symptom: M1L and M1R look identical in the fabric
items.cause: Normal for very fine yarn; the lean is subtle
items.fix: In DK or aran yarn the lean is visible. In lace weight it may only show clearly after blocking. Check the execution by making one increase per method on a swatch and comparing the two columns.
